identity: A 20-item Arabic multiple-choice quiz on Islamic religious knowledge - prophets, companions, suras, and Qur'anic verses. Punctuation stripped; exactly one quiz item per <NL> block, 20 blocks, 447 tokens. Every item is a question stem followed by exactly four answer options set inline with no separators, no option letters, and no marked correct answer. This is register SS (MCQ/quiz) of my doctrine, the same family as doc_1c49614cd6bc and doc_46717e5891d4.
law: The unit is the LAYOUT SLOT, not the printed sentence. One item = [stem] || [option] || [option] || [option] || [option] || <NL>, so 5 boundaries per item, driven by the option list and not by any connective. The stem absorbs everything syntactically inside the question: embedded Qur'anic quotations together with their inline verse numbers, honorific formulas (`عليه السلام`, `صلى الله عليه وسلم`, `رضي الله عنه`), waw-coordinated material (`ولبسها`, `ووهبه للمسلمين`, `والمسلمين`), and trailing subordinate adjuncts (`بعد أن أنجاهم الله من فرعون`). Each option is ONE segment however long - here 1 to 4 tokens - and never splits internally, so nasab chains (X بن Y), construct pairs (`سورة X`, `صحراء X`, `قوم X`, `N آلاف ملك`), noun+adjective compounds (`الأحجار الكريمة`) and name+eulogy pairs stay whole. Free confirmed boundaries: the token before each of the 19 <NL> tokens, plus the final token 446.
reasoning: Step zero of my checklist (identify the unit system before placing any boundary) settles almost the whole document: this is SS, so I hunt for the stem/option layout and give connectives zero weight. In 19 of 20 blocks the four options are recoverable unambiguously because they are parallel in shape, which fixes the stem end by subtraction. Four sites needed real argument. (1) Item 6, tokens 100-114. A five-token option run has to split four ways. `الأحجار الكريمة` is a fixed noun+adjective compound (precious stones) and the semantic set is gold / silver / precious stones / copper, so the split is 110 | 111 | 112-113 | 114, and LAW 3 forbids a cut at 112 inside the modifier. Marked med at 110/111/113 since the four-way split is inferred, not marked. (2) Item 13, tokens 250-269. The options are of unequal length - `يوشع بن نون` / `ذي القرنين` / `هارون` / `الخضر` - including two one-token options. I take the document's four-option regularity over reading `هارون الخضر` as a single option: that is not a name, and all 19 other items have exactly four. Med at 267/268. (3) Item 17, tokens 349-375. The embedded quotation is Nuh 71:10-11 and it carries its verse numbers as literal tokens `10` @362 and `11` @367. SM says a verse number is a boundary that overrides even internal full stops, which would force a cut at 362. I rule SM out: SM is scoped to documents whose whole unit system IS the verse, where the numbers were STRIPPED and the annotators segmented on their positions. Here the numbers SURVIVE as text inside a parenthesised quotation embedded in an MCQ stem, which is the SA2b / checklist-item-3 case - never cut inside a number, a parenthetical, a quotation, or a stem. So no boundary at 362, and the stem-final boundary lands on a digit, @367 = `11`, right before the first option `سورة القصص`. I also tested whether `11` could be an option LETTER welding forward under SS3: it cannot, because there is no 12/13/14 for the other three options and `10` has the identical form mid-quotation. Marked med. (4) The one site I am genuinely unsure of - item 15, tokens 297-325, boundary at 308 `جاثمين`. The pre-option material here is two independent sentences, not one: `قال تعالى في سورة هود` + the verse, then `من هم القوم الذين أهلكهم الله في هذه الآية`. AGAINST cutting: SS1 says the stem is one segment however long and explicitly includes embedded quotations; my batch-2 record in this exact register is 14 false cuts inside stems and zero misses; checklist item 2 says weld at a coin flip. FOR cutting, and this is text-internal evidence rather than instinct: the diagnostic is anaphora direction. In items 14 and 20 the phrase `هذه الآية الكريمة` is CATAphoric - it points forward to a verse that follows inside the same sentence, so the quotation really is embedded and the stem really is one sentence. In item 15 `هذه الآية` is ANAphoric - it points back to a verse already presented, which presupposes that presentation was closed off before the question began. That makes 297-308 a PREAMBLE rather than part of the stem, and the prohibition on cutting inside a stem does not reach a preamble. The cut also falls after the whole quotation, not between the speech verb and its quote, so G1/M2/D3 are untouched - I weld at 301 for exactly that reason. Cost is symmetric here (one error either way), so I follow the text-internal evidence and cut, but record it lo so the grade can settle it. Everything else I welded on doctrine without hesitation: the eulogies `صلى الله عليه وسلم` @185-188 and `رضي الله عنه` @216-218 and the forty-odd `عليه السلام` pairs (A1 - an honorific is bound to its name); `والمسلمين` @189, `ولبسها` @122, `ووهبه` @388 (LAW 1 - waw is never a reason to cut, and SS1/SS2 keep waw-material inside its slot); `فقل` @281, `فيذرها` @285, `فأصبحوا` @305 (LAW 2 - fa is a continuation marker); `بعد أن أنجاهم الله من فرعون` @334-339 (LAW 4 - a trailing subordinate clause belongs to its main clause); and the vocative `يا أيها الناس` @429-431, which superficially looks like a free H3 cut but sits inside a quoted verse inside a stem and is not a conversational turn, so it welds. Totals: 101 boundaries = 19 items x 5 + 6 for item 15. All 19 pre-<NL> tokens and the final token 446 are present.
